serial.parity_note: Must be written QUOTED in config.yaml. An unquoted N parses to boolean False -- the repo parser reads YAML 1.1 false-words {false, no, off, n}. Accepted values are N, E, O only; mark/space are excluded as unverifiable on this board.
serial.provenance: verbatim from the prior working code: ModbusSerialClient('COM3', baudrate=9600, parity='N', stopbits=1, bytesize=8, timeout=1)

unit_id_provenance: inference (library default; never specified in prior code)

setpoint.payload: IEEE-754 float64, byteorder LITTLE, wordorder LITTLE
setpoint.provenance: INFERRED (prior working code only; official meaning unverified)
setpoint.warning: This is NOT the PLC's encoding. The PLC uses float32, byteorder BIG, wordorder LITTLE. Two devices, two encodings -- conflating them produces a well-formed frame carrying a meaningless value, and neither protocol will complain.

command_bound_c.interval: OPEN -- strictly min < value < max; exactly 10.0 and exactly 30.0 are REFUSED
command_bound_c.provenance: MIN IS MEASURED, MAX IS STILL INFERRED -- the two halves no longer share a provenance. min=10.0 was read from the LIVE PLC's `DF21 Temp Output LB` on 2026-09-07 (read-only, five samples, read_holding_registers(28672, count=46), device_id=1, C1 PID Auto OFF, nothing written). The PLC clamps its own temperature-PID output to [10.0, 30.0] C, so that is the range the circulator can legitimately receive. max=30.0 remains INFERRED from the prior system's observed output envelope across all 49,147 logged rows (T output in [0.000, 30.000]); it agrees with the measured DF20 Temp Output UB, but the log envelope on its own is not independent evidence.
command_bound_c.superseded: min was 0.0 until 2026-09-07, INFERRED from the low end of that same log envelope. THE INFERENCE WAS WRONG: the log floor of 0.000 was the prior system's own behaviour, not the PLC's clamp, and the live PLC clamps at 10.0. Do not restore 0.0 from any log-derived argument -- the measurement outranks it.
command_bound_c.code_ceiling_note: tools/circulator/safety.py still carries COMMAND_MIN_C = 0.0 as the widest RANGE the layer will permit, and configs/config.yaml TIGHTENS it to 10.0. The ceiling was left alone deliberately: raising it is a hardware-clearance decision about a board whose own protections are unknown, and DF21 is a fact about the PLC's output, not about what this board tolerates. TODO(operator): decide whether the code ceiling should also become 10.0.
command_bound_c.saturation_artifact: The 2026-01-11 log ends with the temperature output pinned at exactly 30.000 while the measured temperature read 11.4 C -- saturated against the clamp during an aborted run. So 30.000 is a value the BROKEN system produced, which makes it the worst candidate for a legal command.
command_bound_c.why_strict: The MATLAB original enforced Temp SP in (0, 30) as an open interval, refusing exactly 0.0 and 30.0; and the PLC-side setpoint guard is strict too, so no caller has to remember which device behaves which way at its limits. The strictness is unchanged by the measurement: exactly 10.0 is refused for the same reason exactly 30.0 is -- a value sitting precisely on a clamp is what a saturated controller emits.
command_bound_c.why_ours: The board is custom and undocumented, so whether it has an over-temperature cutoff or a setpoint clamp of its own is UNKNOWABLE. Every bound that exists is in tools/circulator/safety.py.
command_bound_c.do_not_mirror: tools/environment/registers.py carries valid_min/valid_max checked INCLUSIVELY, but those are the PLC's SENSOR SCALING bounds (0..100 %RH, -40..180 C) where an exact 100.0 is a legitimate reading. A command bound is a different quantity and is exclusive. CommandLimits is the single source of truth for what may be sent here.
command_bound_c.measured_clamps: tools/environment/registers.py MEASURED_OUTPUT_CLAMPS holds all four PLC output clamps as read on 2026-09-07: DF20 Temp Output UB=30.0 C, DF21 Temp Output LB=10.0 C, DF22 RH Output UB=100.0 %, DF23 RH Output LB=0.0 %. Only the temperature pair bears on this device -- humidity never transits this host.
